ar.nodeRunner.localSyncing: Local node is syncing. Your wallet stays on {{source}} with its current balance until the local node is complete.
ar.nodeRunner.fillingSynced: Synced, but still filling in shielded history from peers{{from}}. Block sync waits for this, so the block count can sit still for a while — it is working, not stuck. The wallet can attach once the node log says "shielded history: VERIFIED" (or the floor drops below your wallet's birthday). Your wallet stays on {{source}} until then.
ar.nodeRunner.fillingSyncing: Local node is syncing and still filling in shielded history from peers{{from}}. Block sync waits for this, so the block count can sit still for a while — it is working, not stuck. The wallet can attach once the node log says "shielded history: VERIFIED" (or the floor drops below your wallet's birthday). Your wallet stays on {{source}} until then.
ar.nodeRunner.walletNotAnswering: The wallet is open, but its selected node is not answering yet. It retries automatically and keeps the last confirmed wallet state visible.
ar.nodeRunner.miningNeverOffered: Mining mode is never offered to the wallet because it does not retain complete historical notes.
ar.selfHost.webIntro: Local process control belongs in the desktop app.
ar.selfHost.webNote: The browser cannot install or supervise programs on your computer. The desktop build keeps services on loopback and restarts managed processes if they fail.
ar.selfHost.title: Local services
ar.selfHost.intro: Private, supervised services on this computer.
ar.selfHost.networkIntro: Use the wallet service from another device and choose how the node participates.
ar.selfHost.pairNote: Scan this in the ZKas wallet app — no tokens to type.
ar.selfHost.pairingAlt: Pairing code for the ZKas wallet app
ar.lockScreen.noReset: There is no way to reset this passphrase — it is never sent anywhere and never stored. If you forget it, the only way back into this wallet is your seed phrase or a backup file, so keep one of those safe.
ar.lockScreen.haveBackup: Already have a backup file? Restore from backup
ar.restoreFromBackup.errDeviceMin: The device passphrase needs at least 8 characters.
ar.restoreFromBackup.errDeviceMismatch: The two device passphrases do not match.
ar.restoreFromBackup.title: Restore from backup
ar.restoreFromBackup.intro: Open an encrypted backup file and set it up on this computer.
ar.restoreFromBackup.filePassPlaceholder: The passphrase you gave the file
ar.restoreFromBackup.rebuildNote: Your balance rebuilds from the chain after restoring — this takes a minute or two.
ar.appLockScreen.wrongSecret: That {{secret}} does not unlock this wallet.
ar.appLockScreen.offerBody: Use your fingerprint to open ZKas instead of typing your {{secret}}. Your {{secret}} still works and is what secures your keys — the fingerprint just unlocks the app on this device, and it never leaves the phone.
ar.appLockScreen.title: Unlock ZKas
ar.appLockScreen.intro: Your wallet key is encrypted on this device. Enter your {{secret}} to use it.
ar.appLockScreen.forgotten: Forgotten it? There is nothing to reset — the {{secret}} is never stored or sent anywhere. The only way back is restoring each wallet from its seed or a backup file.
ar.appLockScreen.wipeWarning: This erases every wallet's data from this device — the coins stay on-chain, but each wallet comes back only from its seed or backup file.
ar.firstRunNode.errEnterAddress: Enter the address of your node (host:port).
ar.firstRunNode.title: Choose how to connect
ar.firstRunNode.intro: Your keys stay on this computer whichever you pick, and your payments stay shielded on the chain. What differs is who can see your activity, and how soon your balance shows.
ar.firstRunNode.optRemote: This computer · public node — runs the wallet here; nothing about your wallet leaves this computer. First sync scans the chain and takes a while.
ar.firstRunNode.optHosted: Public service — ready at once. The wallet service can see your transactions, not your keys.
ar.firstRunNode.optTor: Over Tor — the public service, with your IP hidden. It still sees your transactions. Needs Tor running on this computer.
ar.firstRunNode.optCustom: My own node — a node you already run, anywhere on your network.
ar.firstRunNode.managedLater: You can install and switch to a fully managed local node from the Node page later.
ar.firstRunNode.stillConnecting: Still connecting — it may be slow or busy right now.
ar.firstRunNode.opensNow: Your wallet opens now on the engine on this computer. You can change how it connects under Settings.
ar.firstRunNode.changeLater: You can change this at any time under Settings, without touching your wallet or its balance.
ar.firstRunConnect.errEngine: The on-device engine could not start on this phone.
ar.firstRunConnect.errEnterAddress: Enter the address of your wallet service (host:port, or an .onion).
ar.firstRunConnect.title: Set up your wallet
ar.firstRunConnect.intro: Nothing leaves this device until you tap. Pick where your wallet connects.
ar.firstRunConnect.publicDesc: Fast, nothing to install. The wallet daemon can see your transactions.
ar.firstRunConnect.torDesc: Hides your IP. The daemon still sees your transactions. Needs Orbot.
ar.firstRunConnect.customDesc: A wallet daemon you run yourself.
ar.errorBoundary.title: Something went wrong
ar.errorBoundary.body: The wallet display hit an error. Your wallet and funds are not affected — reloading almost always fixes this.
ar.bootGuard.couldNotStart: The wallet could not start. It needs site storage (cookies / site data) enabled for this site — your wallet and its settings live there. Allow it for {{host}}, then reload.
ar.firstRunConnect.changeLater: You can change any of this later in Settings, without touching your wallet or its balance.
ar.orbotHelp.nativeIntro: The wallet reaches the onion through Orbot, the free Tor app. It isn't running:
ar.orbotHelp.stepInstallIos: Install Orbot from the App Store.
ar.orbotHelp.stepConnectIos: Open it and connect — Orbot runs as a VPN on iPhone, so allow the VPN configuration it asks for.
ar.orbotHelp.stepVpnMode: Open it and turn on VPN mode.
ar.orbotHelp.stepRetry: Come back and tap Connect over Tor again.
ar.orbotHelp.desktopTitle: Tor isn't running on this computer
ar.orbotHelp.desktopIntro: The wallet connects through Tor's own SOCKS port, so nothing has to be routed system-wide — Tor just has to be running. Start the Tor service, or simply open Tor Browser and leave it open, then try again.
ar.orbotHelp.desktopPorts: It looks on 127.0.0.1:9050 (Tor service) and 127.0.0.1:9150 (Tor Browser).
ar.orbotHelp.desktopOwnNode: For privacy without Tor, run your own node from the Node page — then nobody else sees what you ask.
ar.orbotHelp.browserTitle: Open this wallet in Tor Browser
ar.orbotHelp.browserIntro: An ordinary browser cannot reach an .onion address. The whole wallet is served over Tor — open it in Tor Browser at:
ar.orbotHelp.browserKeys: Your keys stay on your device either way.
ar.runOnPhoneOption.title: Run on this phone
ar.runOnPhoneOption.desc: Most private. No daemon ever sees your transactions. A bit more battery.
ar.runOnPhoneOption.nodeHint: Node to sync from — host:port. The default is the public ZKas node.
ar.runOnPhoneOption.torDesc: Hides your IP from the node. Requires the Orbot app (Tor) running on this phone.
ar.whatsNew.title: Recovery phrases
ar.whatsNew.phraseDesc: New wallets use a standard BIP-39 phrase instead of a 64-character seed. Your existing seed keeps working.
ar.whatsNew.accountsDesc: Add accounts from one phrase — one backup covers them all.
ar.whatsNew.torDesc: Connect over an onion so the service never sees your IP.
ar.autoConsolidationCard.offNote: Off. A large payment may need splitting until you merge with Consolidate.
