ko.selfHost.optWanNote: Authenticated backend for a trusted HTTPS reverse proxy or VPN.
ko.selfHost.lanFirewall: Allow inbound TCP {{port}} in the firewall for Private/Home networks only. The app does not change firewall rules or enable UPnP.
ko.selfHost.wanForward: Forward the public HTTPS URL through Caddy, nginx, Tailscale, or Tor to this computer. Do not expose the plain backend port directly to the internet.
ko.selfHost.nodeRpcLanNote: Lets another wallet or miner use TCP {{port}}. No authentication—never forward it to the internet.
ko.selfHost.publicP2pNote: Accept peers on TCP {{port}}. This does not expose wallet data or RPC.
ko.selfHost.stopBeforeApply: Stop the managed node before applying changed node access. Wallet-service changes do not require stopping it.
ko.selfHost.walletEngineNote: Sync and proving API embedded in this app.
ko.selfHost.boundNote: Bound to this device. The app token is never shown or forwarded.
ko.selfHost.explorerNote: Local chain REST API and transaction index.
ko.selfHost.dataApiNote: Data API, not a web page — the address itself returns 404. Try {{url}}/info/blockdag.
ko.selfHost.lastExit: Last exit: {{exit}} — if the wallet's Explore tab still works, another copy is already serving this port. Use View logs for the exact reason.
ko.selfHost.dataBackupNote: Wallet backups contain the irreplaceable key. Node chain data and the explorer index are intentionally not copied—they are large, public, and can be rebuilt.
ko.selfHost.startupNote: Start the app with your computer. An encrypted wallet still opens locked.
ko.selfHost.trayNote: Closing the window keeps active node or mining services in the tray, but immediately locks the spending engine. Use “Quit and stop services” in the tray to stop every child process.
ko.dashboardView.liveUnavailable: Live data is temporarily unavailable. Showing the last saved snapshot.
ko.dashboardView.notResponding: The explorer API is not responding.
ko.dashboardView.title: Network
ko.dashboardView.intro: Public chain facts. Payment details remain private.
ko.dashboardView.tailNote: The schedule ends in a permanent tail emission; it has no fixed terminal supply.
ko.blockView.title: Block
ko.transactionView.title: Transaction
ko.transactionView.privateNote: The public chain proves this transaction is valid. It does not reveal the sender, recipient, or transferred amount.
ko.addressView.title: Shielded address
ko.addressView.invalid: This is not a valid-looking ZKAS address.
ko.addressView.noPublicNote: ZKAS addresses do not have transparent explorer pages. Only the holder's viewing key can discover received notes, amounts, and transaction history.
ko.lockScreen.errMismatch: The two passphrases do not match.
ko.lockScreen.unlockIntro: Your seed is encrypted on this device. Enter your passphrase to unlock it.
ko.lockScreen.plaintextIntro: This wallet's seed is currently stored unencrypted on this computer — anyone with access to the file could spend your funds. Set a passphrase now and it will be encrypted in place. Your balance and history are not affected.
ko.lockScreen.chooseIntro: Choose a passphrase. It encrypts your wallet's seed on this computer, so the files left on disk are useless to anyone who copies them.
ko.lockScreen.noReset: There is no way to reset this passphrase — it is never sent anywhere and never stored. If you forget it, the only way back into this wallet is your seed phrase or a backup file, so keep one of those safe.
ko.lockScreen.haveBackup: Already have a backup file? Restore from backup
ko.restoreFromBackup.errDeviceMin: The device passphrase needs at least 8 characters.
ko.restoreFromBackup.errDeviceMismatch: The two device passphrases do not match.
ko.restoreFromBackup.title: Restore from backup
ko.restoreFromBackup.intro: Open an encrypted backup file and set it up on this computer.
ko.restoreFromBackup.filePassPlaceholder: The passphrase you gave the file
ko.restoreFromBackup.rebuildNote: Your balance rebuilds from the chain after restoring — this takes a minute or two.
ko.appLockScreen.wrongSecret: That {{secret}} does not unlock this wallet.
ko.appLockScreen.offerBody: Use your fingerprint to open ZKas instead of typing your {{secret}}. Your {{secret}} still works and is what secures your keys — the fingerprint just unlocks the app on this device, and it never leaves the phone.
ko.appLockScreen.title: Unlock ZKas
ko.errorBoundary.title: Something went wrong
ko.errorBoundary.body: The wallet display hit an error. Your wallet and funds are not affected — reloading almost always fixes this.
ko.bootGuard.couldNotStart: The wallet could not start. It needs site storage (cookies / site data) enabled for this site — your wallet and its settings live there. Allow it for {{host}}, then reload.
ko.appLockScreen.intro: Your wallet key is encrypted on this device. Enter your {{secret}} to use it.
ko.appLockScreen.forgotten: Forgotten it? There is nothing to reset — the {{secret}} is never stored or sent anywhere. The only way back is restoring each wallet from its seed or a backup file.
ko.appLockScreen.wipeWarning: This erases every wallet's data from this device — the coins stay on-chain, but each wallet comes back only from its seed or backup file.
ko.firstRunNode.errEnterAddress: Enter the address of your node (host:port).
ko.firstRunNode.title: Choose how to connect
ko.firstRunNode.intro: Your keys stay on this computer whichever you pick, and your payments stay shielded on the chain. What differs is who can see your activity, and how soon your balance shows.
ko.firstRunNode.optRemote: This computer · public node — runs the wallet here; nothing about your wallet leaves this computer. First sync scans the chain and takes a while.
ko.firstRunNode.optHosted: Public service — ready at once. The wallet service can see your transactions, not your keys.
ko.firstRunNode.optTor: Over Tor — the public service, with your IP hidden. It still sees your transactions. Needs Tor running on this computer.
ko.firstRunNode.optCustom: My own node — a node you already run, anywhere on your network.
ko.firstRunNode.managedLater: You can install and switch to a fully managed local node from the Node page later.
ko.firstRunNode.stillConnecting: Still connecting — it may be slow or busy right now.
ko.firstRunNode.opensNow: Your wallet opens now on the engine on this computer. You can change how it connects under Settings.
ko.firstRunNode.changeLater: You can change this at any time under Settings, without touching your wallet or its balance.
ko.firstRunConnect.errEngine: The on-device engine could not start on this phone.
ko.firstRunConnect.errEnterAddress: Enter the address of your wallet service (host:port, or an .onion).
ko.firstRunConnect.title: Set up your wallet
ko.firstRunConnect.intro: Nothing leaves this device until you tap. Pick where your wallet connects.
ko.firstRunConnect.publicDesc: Fast, nothing to install. The wallet daemon can see your transactions.
ko.firstRunConnect.torDesc: Hides your IP. The daemon still sees your transactions. Needs Orbot.
ko.firstRunConnect.customDesc: A wallet daemon you run yourself.
ko.firstRunConnect.changeLater: You can change any of this later in Settings, without touching your wallet or its balance.
ko.orbotHelp.nativeIntro: The wallet reaches the onion through Orbot, the free Tor app. It isn't running:
ko.orbotHelp.stepInstallIos: Install Orbot from the App Store.
ko.orbotHelp.stepConnectIos: Open it and connect — Orbot runs as a VPN on iPhone, so allow the VPN configuration it asks for.
ko.orbotHelp.stepVpnMode: Open it and turn on VPN mode.
ko.orbotHelp.stepRetry: Come back and tap Connect over Tor again.
ko.orbotHelp.desktopTitle: Tor isn't running on this computer
ko.orbotHelp.desktopIntro: The wallet connects through Tor's own SOCKS port, so nothing has to be routed system-wide — Tor just has to be running. Start the Tor service, or simply open Tor Browser and leave it open, then try again.
ko.orbotHelp.desktopPorts: It looks on 127.0.0.1:9050 (Tor service) and 127.0.0.1:9150 (Tor Browser).
ko.orbotHelp.desktopOwnNode: For privacy without Tor, run your own node from the Node page — then nobody else sees what you ask.
ko.orbotHelp.browserTitle: Open this wallet in Tor Browser
ko.orbotHelp.browserIntro: An ordinary browser cannot reach an .onion address. The whole wallet is served over Tor — open it in Tor Browser at:
ko.orbotHelp.browserKeys: Your keys stay on your device either way.
ko.runOnPhoneOption.title: Run on this phone
ko.runOnPhoneOption.desc: Most private. No daemon ever sees your transactions. A bit more battery.
ko.runOnPhoneOption.nodeHint: Node to sync from — host:port. The default is the public ZKas node.
ko.runOnPhoneOption.torDesc: Hides your IP from the node. Requires the Orbot app (Tor) running on this phone.
ko.whatsNew.title: Recovery phrases
ko.whatsNew.phraseDesc: New wallets use a standard BIP-39 phrase instead of a 64-character seed. Your existing seed keeps working.
ko.whatsNew.accountsDesc: Add accounts from one phrase — one backup covers them all.
ko.whatsNew.torDesc: Connect over an onion so the service never sees your IP.

it.verify.reasonMismatch: signature does not verify for this address/message
it.verify.valid: ✓ VALID — the signer controls this address.
it.history.title: History
it.history.recovering: Recovering your history from the chain — a minute or two. You can leave this tab.
it.history.empty: Nothing yet. Payments you receive and send show up here.
it.history.sentPrivately: Sent privately. Watch it confirm below — this updates live.
it.history.noticedOnOpen: Noticed when you opened the app
it.send.needSeed: This device doesn't hold this wallet's key yet. Enter your recovery phrase once to unlock sending here.
it.send.wrongSeed: That seed belongs to a different wallet — it does not unlock this one. Check which wallet you are restoring, or switch to the wallet that seed belongs to.
it.send.partialRecorded: {{message}} The part already broadcast is recorded in History.
it.send.manyNotes: Your balance sits in {{n}} notes. If this amount cannot fit in one transaction, nothing is sent and the wallet will offer consolidation or an explicit split payment.
it.send.memoSealed: “{{memo}}” — sealed in the recipient's encrypted note; only they can read it.
it.send.warmingNote: ⚡ This first payment will take a few minutes — the wallet has to locate your coins in the chain before it can spend them. It only does this once; later payments take seconds.
it.send.signedOnDevice: Verified and signed on your device, then broadcast. Usually takes a few seconds.
it.send.chooseSafely: Choose safely: consolidation is recommended. “Send in parts” broadcasts independent transactions; accepted parts cannot be automatically reversed if a later part fails.
it.send.consolidationSentBody: Wait for the new note to mature, then retry the full payment.
it.send.splitProgress: Your balance is spread across many small notes, so this payment is being sent as {{parts}} transactions — {{sent}} of {{total}} ZKAS confirmed so far. Keep this page open until it finishes.
it.send.title: Send
it.send.clipboardEmptyBody: Copy the address first, then tap Paste.
it.send.clipboardBlockedTitle: This browser won't share the clipboard
it.send.clipboardBlockedBody: Press and hold the address field, then choose Paste.
it.send.badAddress: That doesn't look like a zkas: address.
it.send.selfAddress: That's your own address. The payment works — it just returns to you, minus the fee.
it.send.feeHint: Leave empty and the wallet picks the fee. Raise it only after a fee error.
it.send.memoHint: Sealed inside the recipient's encrypted note — only they can read it. Never appears on-chain or on the explorer.
it.send.maturingHint: Only {{spendable}} is ready to spend right now — {{maturing}} is still arriving. Coins become spendable about 10 minutes after they land, including the change from a payment you just made. It'll be ready shortly.
it.send.notEnough: Not enough funds: {{spendable}} spendable, need {{need}} incl. up to {{maxFee}} fee.
it.send.feeSummary: + {{min}}–{{max}} fee (scales with how many coins get combined) = up to {{total}} total
it.send.catchingUp: Still catching up with the chain — you can pay once it finishes, so the wallet knows about all your coins.
it.send.warmBanner:
⚡ Your first payment will take a few minutes.
Locating your coins — this happens once. You can start the payment now.
it.sign.title: Sign message
it.sign.intro: Prove you control this wallet's address without spending. The signature discloses your viewing key (enables note detection, never spend authority).
it.verify.title: Verify message
it.verify.intro: Runs entirely in your browser — no server involved.
it.history.held_one: {{count}} outgoing transaction in flight — {{amount}} ZKAS temporarily held until it confirms (returned automatically within ~1 hour if it never does).
it.history.held_other: {{count}} outgoing transactions in flight — {{amount}} ZKAS temporarily held until it confirms (returned automatically within ~1 hour if it never does).
it.history.rescanHint: Re-read the chain to rebuild this history and recover any funds the local view lost.
it.history.recoveredNote: Recovered from the chain by your viewing key. Tap a payment for details.
it.history.exportFailed: Could not export the CSV on this device.
it.history.turnOffBody: Erases the stored transaction list only. Your balance and funds are unaffected.
it.daemonSetting.unreachable: Couldn't reach a wallet service at {{url}} ({{detail}}). Make sure zkas-walletd is running there and the port is open. Nothing was changed — still using {{current}}.
it.daemonSetting.title: Connect to your own node
it.daemonSetting.intro: Your seed always signs on this device. But the hosted service still sees your viewing key — it can watch your balance and history. To keep even that private, run zkas-walletd on your own node and connect this wallet straight to it.
it.daemonSetting.enterIp: Just enter your node's IP address — we add the rest.
it.daemonSetting.nativeTransports: The installed app supports HTTPS and plain HTTP LAN connections.
it.daemonSetting.webTransports: The web wallet requires HTTPS; use the installed app for plain HTTP on a LAN.
it.daemonSetting.portNote: Uses port {{port}} by default — add :port only if you changed it.
it.vaultSetting.title: Security & backup
it.vaultSetting.plaintextWarning: This wallet's seed is stored unencrypted on this computer — anyone who copies the file can spend your funds. Set a passphrase to encrypt it; your balance and history are untouched.
it.vaultSetting.lockingNote: Locking stops the daemon and forgets your passphrase until you re-enter it.
it.vaultSetting.lockBody: The wallet daemon stops and your passphrase is forgotten. You will need it again to unlock. Your funds are not affected.
it.autoConsolidationCard.title: Automatic consolidation
it.autoConsolidationCard.intro: Occasionally merges your oldest notes in the background so a payment always fits. Each merge costs a small fee — turn it off to merge yourself with Consolidate instead.
it.autoConsolidationCard.offNote: Off. A large payment may need splitting until you merge with Consolidate.
it.debugLogsCard.title: Debug logs
it.debugLogsCard.verboseHint: More detail from the on-device engine. Turn on when a wallet is stuck opening or a send fails, then Show engine logs.
it.debugLogsCard.noLogs: No logs yet — the engine may not be running.
it.networkPrivacyCard.title: Network privacy
it.networkPrivacyCard.desktopNote: Keys stay in this app. Strongest privacy: run your own node (Node page). You can also connect over Tor if Tor is running on this computer — both from Chain source above.
it.networkPrivacyCard.enterAddress: Enter a wallet-service address (host:port or an .onion).
it.networkPrivacyCard.intro: What your wallet connects to. Tap to switch.
it.networkPrivacyCard.publicHint: Fast. The wallet daemon can see your transactions.
it.networkPrivacyCard.torHint: Hides your IP. The daemon still sees your transactions. Needs Orbot.
it.networkPrivacyCard.customHint: A wallet daemon you run yourself.
it.backgroundSyncCard.title: Background sync
it.backgroundSyncCard.intro: While on, the phone wakes about every 15 min (even closed) to stay synced and notify you of payments. Off, it catches up when you open the app. The seed stays on this device either way.
it.backgroundSyncCard.onNote: On. Android may delay the wake when the battery is low — payments are never lost, the notification is simply later.
it.biometricToggle.linkIntroPin: Enter your current PIN once to link it to this device's fingerprint. It stays sealed on the device; the fingerprint only releases it to open the app.
it.biometricToggle.linkIntroPassphrase: Enter your current passphrase once to link it to this device's fingerprint. It stays sealed on the device; the fingerprint only releases it to open the app.
it.biometricToggle.isOn: Fingerprint unlock is on. Open the app with a fingerprint instead of typing.
it.biometricToggle.offerPin: Unlock with a fingerprint instead of typing your PIN.
it.biometricToggle.offerPassphrase: Unlock with a fingerprint instead of typing your passphrase.
it.appLockSetting.mismatch: The two entries do not match.
it.appLockSetting.wrongSecret: That passphrase does not unlock this device.
it.appLockSetting.title: App lock
it.appLockSetting.enableIntro: Choose what to unlock with. This encrypts the key of every wallet on this device and asks for it when the app opens — while locked, this device holds nothing that can spend any of them.
it.appLockSetting.alsoBioPin: Also unlock with fingerprint (you'll scan it once to link). Your PIN keeps working.
it.appLockSetting.alsoBioPassphrase: Also unlock with fingerprint (you'll scan it once to link). Your passphrase keeps working.
it.appLockSetting.backupFirstPin: Back up your wallet first. Nothing stores this PIN, so if you forget it the only way back in is your seed phrase or a backup file.
it.appLockSetting.backupFirstPassphrase: Back up your wallet first. Nothing stores this passphrase, so if you forget it the only way back in is your seed phrase or a backup file.
it.appLockSetting.pinStrength: A PIN stops someone who picks up your phone. Use a passphrase for stronger protection.
it.appLockSetting.disableIntroPin: Enter your current PIN to turn the lock off. Your key will be stored unencrypted on this device again.
it.appLockSetting.disableIntroPassphrase: Enter your current passphrase to turn the lock off. Your key will be stored unencrypted on this device again.
it.appLockSetting.onNotePin: On. Every wallet's key on this device is encrypted, and the app asks for your PIN to open. It re-locks itself after a few minutes in the background.
it.appLockSetting.onNotePassphrase: On. Every wallet's key on this device is encrypted, and the app asks for your passphrase to open. It re-locks itself after a few minutes in the background.
it.appLockSetting.offIntro: Your wallet keys are stored on this device unencrypted. Turn on a PIN or passphrase and every one of them is encrypted at rest, and the app asks for it on open — so someone holding this device, or a backup of its data, cannot spend from it.
it.switchWallet.title: Wallets
it.switchWallet.intro: This device can hold several wallets at once. Switching between them keeps every one of them — their keys, history and contacts stay exactly where they are.
it.switchWallet.removeBody: This wallet's key and data are erased from this device. Your other wallets are not affected. The coins stay on-chain but are unreachable from here without a backup or seed phrase.
it.renameWallet.title: Rename wallet
it.deviceSeedBackup.noKey: This device holds no spending key for the wallet — it can watch the balance but not spend. Restore your seed phrase on the Send tab to spend from here.
it.deviceSeedBackup.mismatch: The two passphrases do not match.
it.deviceSeedBackup.copied: Your backup is copied. Paste it somewhere safe now — a password manager or a note to yourself.
it.deviceSeedBackup.written: Backup written. Keep it off this computer. It is encrypted, useless without the passphrase.
it.deviceSeedBackup.intro: Back up your wallet. Save an encrypted copy so you can restore this wallet if the machine is lost.
it.deviceSeedBackup.loseWarning: Lose the backup passphrase and the file cannot be opened — not by us, not by anyone. Your seed phrase remains the other way back in.
it.restoreSeedBackup.wrongWallet: That backup belongs to a different wallet than the one open now, so it was not applied — restoring it here would overwrite this wallet's key. Use “Add separate wallet”, then restore the backup there.
it.restoreSeedBackup.storeFailed: This device could not store the wallet key — free up space and try again.
it.restoreSeedBackup.restored: Wallet restored. Your balance rebuilds from the chain — this takes a minute or two.
it.restoreSeedBackup.intro: Restore from backup. Open an encrypted backup file and put its wallet on this computer.
it.restoreSeedBackup.passPlaceholder: The passphrase you gave the file
it.backupWallet.mismatch: The two passphrases do not match.
it.backupWallet.written: Backup written. Keep it off this computer — a USB stick or password manager. It is encrypted.
it.backupWallet.intro: Backup — save an encrypted copy of your wallet to a file. Restore it on any computer with this app. Give it its own passphrase; do not reuse the one that unlocks this device.
it.backupWallet.loseWarning: Lose this passphrase and the file cannot be opened — not by us, not by anyone. Your seed phrase remains the other way back in.
it.nodeSourceSetting.title: Wallet node
it.nodeSourceSetting.intro: The embedded wallet engine keeps your keys on this computer. Node changes are checked before the wallet switches.
it.desktopEngineDown.startingTitle: Starting the wallet on this computer
it.desktopEngineDown.startingBody: Loading your wallet and catching up to the chain. The first run takes a few minutes; it keeps going if you close this.
it.desktopEngineDown.lostTitle: Lost the connection to the wallet on this computer
it.desktopEngineDown.notStartedTitle: The wallet on this computer didn't start
it.desktopEngineDown.lostBody: The wallet is running on this computer but stopped answering. Retry reconnects to it.
it.desktopEngineDown.notStartedBody: The wallet that runs on this computer isn't answering. Your coins are safe on the chain — this is only how the app is reading them.
it.desktopEngineDown.publicHint: You can use the public wallet service instead: it has already scanned the chain, so nothing has to start or sync here.
it.desktopEngineDown.retryHint: If retrying does not help, the public wallet service above needs nothing running on this computer. You can switch back to running it here later, from Chain source.
it.setup.title: Can't reach the wallet service
it.setup.nativeDown: The wallet service isn't responding. Check your connection and try again shortly — your funds are safe on-chain.
it.setup.hostedDown: The hosted wallet service isn't responding. Nothing for you to run — try again shortly.
it.setup.privacyNote: Your spending key is on this device either way — it is never sent to the service. What running your own zkas-walletd changes is privacy: the hosted service can see which wallet is asking about which blocks, and your own daemon sees only what you already know.
it.setup.nativeTransports: The installed app accepts HTTPS and plain HTTP LAN addresses.
it.setup.webTransports: The web wallet requires an HTTPS wallet-service URL.
it.sendScene.warmingCaption: Preparing: locating your coins in the chain{{details}} — done once, never again
it.sendScene.signingCaption: Signing on your device — your key never leaves it
it.sendScene.broadcastingCaption: Sealed and shielded — broadcasting to the network
it.sendScene.slowCaption: Locating your coins in the chain — this can take a minute or two
it.sendScene.provingCaption: Building your zero-knowledge proof — nobody will see amount or recipient
it.sendScene.reassure: Nothing has been sent yet and nothing can be lost — keep this open.
it.appearanceCard.title: Accent color
it.appearanceCard.intro: Balance, buttons and highlights. Teal is the ZKas signature.
it.signatures.title: Signatures
it.signatures.intro: Prove you control your address without spending from it, or check somebody else's proof.
it.aboutCard.title: About
it.aboutCard.blurb: ZKas Wallet — every balance and payment shielded by Orchard zero-knowledge proofs. Your spending key is held on this device and never sent anywhere.
it.contactPicker.title: Choose a contact
it.contactPicker.empty: No contacts yet. Save one after a payment, or from a received address — on a shielded chain the wallet is the only place an address can have a name.
it.saveContactDialog.title: Save contact
it.saveContactDialog.name: Name
it.txDetail.explorerNote: The explorer shows only that a shielded transaction happened — never its details.
it.accessTokenSetting.title: Show access-token field
it.accessTokenSetting.detail: Adds a token box to wallet-server setup. Only needed for a token-protected wallet server.
it.watchOnAnotherDevice.noKey: This device does not hold the key for this wallet.
it.watchOnAnotherDevice.intro: Your view key lets another device or tool watch this wallet — balance and history, read-only. It can never send.
it.watchOnAnotherDevice.warn: Anyone with this key sees every amount and memo this wallet has ever had, and everything it receives from now on — you can't undo that without moving your coins.
it.watchOnAnotherDevice.otherDevice: On the other device: open the wallet → Watch a wallet, then paste this key (or scan the QR).
it.stopWatching.intro: This device holds a view key and no spending key, so it can show the balance and history and cannot send. Nothing here can move coins.
it.stopWatching.warn: Removes the view key from this browser. Anyone else holding the link keeps their view — that can only be ended by moving the coins.
it.saveContactDialog.storedOnDevice: Stored only on this device — a list of who you pay is exactly the metadata ZKas exists to protect.
it.contactsCard.title: Contacts
it.contactsCard.empty: Nobody saved yet. Naming an address here is the only way it will ever read as a person — the chain itself knows nothing about who anyone is.
it.editContact.name: Name
it.editContact.removeBody: Only the name is forgotten — any payments you made are untouched, and the address itself stays in your history.
it.rescanButton.offHint: Recovers your balance from the chain. History is off, so this rebuilds funds — not a transaction list.
it.rescanButton.rescanning: Rescanning — this tab updates as it catches up.
it.qrScanner.hint: Point the camera at the recipient's address QR code
it.requestAmount.hint: The payer's wallet fills in the amount and note — they can still change them.
it.receive.title: Receive
it.receive.seedMoved: Looking for your recovery seed? It moved to Settings → Recovery seed, behind your app lock.
it.revealSeedCard.noKey: This device doesn't hold this wallet's key — it is never sent to the server. Restore it with your recovery phrase or backup.
it.revealSeedCard.introPhrase: These words restore this wallet and every account under it. Reveal only somewhere private.
it.revealSeedCard.introSeed: This seed is the only way to restore this wallet. Reveal only somewhere private.
it.revealSeedCard.privateWarn: Make sure nobody can see your screen. The next tap puts your spending key on it.
it.revealSeedCard.keepPrivate: Keep this private. Anyone with it controls your funds.
it.qrScanner.denied: Camera permission was denied. Allow camera access, or paste the address instead.
it.qrScanner.noCamera: No camera found on this device — paste the address instead.
it.qrScanner.failed: Couldn't start the camera. Paste the address instead.
it.iosInstallNotice.installedCopy: Have a wallet in Safari? It is not shared with this installed copy — restore it here from its recovery phrase.
it.iosInstallNotice.beforeInstall: Installing to your Home Screen starts a separate, empty copy — back up your recovery phrase first, then restore it in the installed app.
it.connectionButton.engineStartFailed: The on-device engine could not start.
it.connectionButton.introDesktop: Your keys stay on this device either way. Use the public service for a wallet that is ready at once, or run the wallet here and pick the node it reads the chain from.
it.connectionButton.introMobile: Your keys stay on this device. Choose how it connects.
it.connectionButton.publicDescDesktop: Ready at once. The wallet daemon can see your transactions.
it.connectionButton.publicDescMobile: Fast. The wallet daemon can see your transactions.
it.connectionButton.thisComputerPublicDesc: Runs the wallet here. First sync scans the chain and takes a while.
it.connectionButton.torDescDesktop: Hides your IP. The daemon still sees your transactions. Needs Tor.
it.connectionButton.torDescMobile: Hides your IP. The daemon still sees your transactions. Needs Orbot.
it.connectionButton.addOwnDesc: A wallet daemon you run yourself.
it.connectionButton.notPairingCode: That code is not a wallet-service pairing code. On the computer serving the wallet, open Host → Network access → Pair a phone.
it.connectionButton.nodeNotInstalled: Managed local node is not installed yet. The Mine and Node screens can install the verified release automatically.
it.walletSwitcher.title: Your wallets
it.walletSwitcher.hintAccounts: Accounts share your phrase. Restoring on a new device? Add account brings each one back, in order.
it.walletSwitcher.hintSeparate: A separate wallet gets its own recovery phrase.
it.recoverHistoryDialog.title: Recover full history
it.recoverHistoryDialog.intro: Details are saved with this wallet, so anyone with its data can read them.
it.recoverHistoryDialog.knowWhenHint: Scan from that date. Much faster.
it.recoverHistoryDialog.heightKnown: Block height this wallet started at
it.recoverHistoryDialog.scanningFromDays_on: Scanning from DAA {{from}} — about {{count}} day of chain.
it.recoverHistoryDialog.scanningFromDays_ot: Scanning from DAA {{from}} — about {{count}} days of chain.
it.recoverHistoryDialog.scanningWhole: Scanning the whole chain. This finds everything, and takes the longest.
it.consolidateDialog.errEnterSeed: Enter this wallet's 64-character recovery seed to sign on this device.
it.consolidateDialog.errWrongSeed: That seed belongs to a different wallet.
it.consolidateDialog.errNoAddress: This wallet has no address yet.
it.consolidateDialog.title: Manage notes
it.consolidateDialog.done: Done. Ready to spend after they settle (about 10 minutes).
it.consolidateDialog.more: Open this again once they settle to keep going.

it.mining.heroText: Rewards go straight to this wallet — there is no pool account and no fee. The app installs what is missing, starts the node, and keeps it running.
it.batchSend.title: Batch send
it.batchSend.intro: One recipient per line: address, amount, optional memo. walletd packs recipients into as few proofs as consensus allows.
it.batchSend.invalidLine: Line {{line}} has an invalid address or amount.
it.batchSend.feeError: Enter a positive fee with at most 8 decimal places.
it.batchSend.feeNote: Automatic is recommended. The node raises a low value to the byte-proportional relay minimum; paying more does not buy a faster lane.
it.batchSend.custodial: Batch send needs a self-hosted walletd that holds this wallet's seed. This app will not upload your seed to enable it.
it.walletMaintenance.title: Notes
it.walletMaintenance.intro: Fewer notes make large payments cheaper and faster to prove.
it.walletMaintenance.warning: Do not consolidate a normal wallet just to make the count smaller: it costs a real fee and creates an on-chain transaction. It is useful for mining and payout wallets with hundreds of small matured notes.
it.mining.lanPreferred: Preferred · try another if your ASIC uses it

it.mining.startToReceive: Start mining to receive ASIC work.
it.mining.nodeSyncingWarning: The ZKAS node is syncing. Keep the app running; the bridge is supervised and mining becomes ready when the node catches up.

it.nodeStartDialog.title: Choose how to run it
it.nodeStartDialog.miningNote: Smallest. Validates the chain and serves miners, but does not keep old wallet notes.
it.nodeStartDialog.shieldedNote: Keeps complete wallet history while pruning old full block bodies.
it.nodeStartDialog.archiveNote: Keeps complete wallet history and every block body. Uses the most disk.
it.nodeStartDialog.inboundNote: Optional. Other nodes can connect to this computer on TCP port {{port}}.
it.nodeStartDialog.firewallPublic: Allow inbound TCP {{port}} in the operating-system firewall. If this machine is behind a router, forward {{port}} only if you want public inbound peers.
it.nodeStartDialog.firewallPrivate: The node makes outbound peer connections and will sync normally. Its P2P listener stays on this device.
it.nodeStartDialog.rpcPrivate: Node RPC is private by default. Trusted-LAN access can be enabled in Host; never expose TCP {{port}} to the internet.
it.nodeStartDialog.miningConflict: This wallet currently uses the local node. Switch the wallet to its public service before running the history-free Mining mode.
it.nodeRunner.webNote: A phone or browser cannot safely keep a full node running. The wallet still works through its selected node.
it.nodeRunner.title: Your ZKAS node
it.nodeRunner.intro: Private wallet access and direct mining, managed by this app.
it.nodeRunner.installNote: The verified ZKAS release is downloaded into the app's private data folder.
it.nodeRunner.updateNote: {{release}} fixes fresh-node synchronization and shielded-history transfer.
it.nodeRunner.rpcNotReady: The process is running but RPC is not ready yet: {{error}}
it.nodeRunner.walletSeparate: The wallet is separate from the node process above.
it.selfHost.pairingWarning: Anyone who scans this gets full access to this wallet. Treat it like the recovery seed.
it.selfHost.optDeviceNote: Random loopback port. Nothing else can connect.
it.selfHost.optLanNote: Authenticated service for desktop and mobile apps on a trusted LAN.
it.selfHost.optWanNote: Authenticated backend for a trusted HTTPS reverse proxy or VPN.
it.selfHost.lanFirewall: Allow inbound TCP {{port}} in the firewall for Private/Home networks only. The app does not change firewall rules or enable UPnP.
it.selfHost.wanForward: Forward the public HTTPS URL through Caddy, nginx, Tailscale, or Tor to this computer. Do not expose the plain backend port directly to the internet.
it.selfHost.nodeRpcLanNote: Lets another wallet or miner use TCP {{port}}. No authentication—never forward it to the internet.
it.selfHost.publicP2pNote: Accept peers on TCP {{port}}. This does not expose wallet data or RPC.
it.selfHost.stopBeforeApply: Stop the managed node before applying changed node access. Wallet-service changes do not require stopping it.
it.selfHost.walletEngineNote: Sync and proving API embedded in this app.
it.selfHost.boundNote: Bound to this device. The app token is never shown or forwarded.
it.nodeRunner.localSyncing: Local node is syncing. Your wallet stays on {{source}} with its current balance until the local node is complete.
it.nodeRunner.fillingSynced: Synced, but still filling in shielded history from peers{{from}}. Block sync waits for this, so the block count can sit still for a while — it is working, not stuck. The wallet can attach once the node log says "shielded history: VERIFIED" (or the floor drops below your wallet's birthday). Your wallet stays on {{source}} until then.
it.nodeRunner.fillingSyncing: Local node is syncing and still filling in shielded history from peers{{from}}. Block sync waits for this, so the block count can sit still for a while — it is working, not stuck. The wallet can attach once the node log says "shielded history: VERIFIED" (or the floor drops below your wallet's birthday). Your wallet stays on {{source}} until then.
it.nodeRunner.walletNotAnswering: The wallet is open, but its selected node is not answering yet. It retries automatically and keeps the last confirmed wallet state visible.
it.nodeRunner.miningNeverOffered: Mining mode is never offered to the wallet because it does not retain complete historical notes.
it.selfHost.webIntro: Local process control belongs in the desktop app.
it.selfHost.webNote: The browser cannot install or supervise programs on your computer. The desktop build keeps services on loopback and restarts managed processes if they fail.
it.selfHost.title: Local services
it.selfHost.intro: Private, supervised services on this computer.
it.selfHost.networkIntro: Use the wallet service from another device and choose how the node participates.
it.selfHost.pairNote: Scan this in the ZKas wallet app — no tokens to type.
it.selfHost.pairingAlt: Pairing code for the ZKas wallet app
it.selfHost.explorerNote: Local chain REST API and transaction index.
it.selfHost.dataApiNote: Data API, not a web page — the address itself returns 404. Try {{url}}/info/blockdag.
it.selfHost.lastExit: Last exit: {{exit}} — if the wallet's Explore tab still works, another copy is already serving this port. Use View logs for the exact reason.
it.selfHost.dataBackupNote: Wallet backups contain the irreplaceable key. Node chain data and the explorer index are intentionally not copied—they are large, public, and can be rebuilt.
it.selfHost.startupNote: Start the app with your computer. An encrypted wallet still opens locked.
it.selfHost.trayNote: Closing the window keeps active node or mining services in the tray, but immediately locks the spending engine. Use “Quit and stop services” in the tray to stop every child process.

it.lockScreen.haveBackup: Already have a backup file? Restore from backup

it.restoreFromBackup.filePassPlaceholder: The passphrase you gave the file

it.appLockScreen.wrongSecret: That {{secret}} does not unlock this wallet.
it.appLockScreen.offerBody: Use your fingerprint to open ZKas instead of typing your {{secret}}. Your {{secret}} still works and is what secures your keys — the fingerprint just unlocks the app on this device, and it never leaves the phone.

it.addressView.noPublicNote: ZKAS addresses do not have transparent explorer pages. Only the holder's viewing key can discover received notes, amounts, and transaction history.
it.lockScreen.errMismatch: The two passphrases do not match.
it.lockScreen.unlockIntro: Your seed is encrypted on this device. Enter your passphrase to unlock it.
it.lockScreen.plaintextIntro: This wallet's seed is currently stored unencrypted on this computer — anyone with access to the file could spend your funds. Set a passphrase now and it will be encrypted in place. Your balance and history are not affected.
it.lockScreen.chooseIntro: Choose a passphrase. It encrypts your wallet's seed on this computer, so the files left on disk are useless to anyone who copies them.

it.errorBoundary.body: The wallet display hit an error. Your wallet and funds are not affected — reloading almost always fixes this.
it.bootGuard.couldNotStart: The wallet could not start. It needs site storage (cookies / site data) enabled for this site — your wallet and its settings live there. Allow it for {{host}}, then reload.
it.appLockScreen.intro: Your wallet key is encrypted on this device. Enter your {{secret}} to use it.
it.appLockScreen.forgotten: Forgotten it? There is nothing to reset — the {{secret}} is never stored or sent anywhere. The only way back is restoring each wallet from its seed or a backup file.
it.appLockScreen.wipeWarning: This erases every wallet's data from this device — the coins stay on-chain, but each wallet comes back only from its seed or backup file.
it.firstRunNode.errEnterAddress: Enter the address of your node (host:port).
it.firstRunNode.title: Choose how to connect
it.firstRunNode.intro: Your keys stay on this computer whichever you pick, and your payments stay shielded on the chain. What differs is who can see your activity, and how soon your balance shows.
it.firstRunNode.optRemote: This computer · public node — runs the wallet here; nothing about your wallet leaves this computer. First sync scans the chain and takes a while.
it.firstRunNode.optHosted: Public service — ready at once. The wallet service can see your transactions, not your keys.
it.firstRunNode.optTor: Over Tor — the public service, with your IP hidden. It still sees your transactions. Needs Tor running on this computer.
it.firstRunNode.optCustom: My own node — a node you already run, anywhere on your network.
it.firstRunNode.managedLater: You can install and switch to a fully managed local node from the Node page later.
it.firstRunNode.stillConnecting: Still connecting — it may be slow or busy right now.
it.firstRunNode.opensNow: Your wallet opens now on the engine on this computer. You can change how it connects under Settings.
it.firstRunNode.changeLater: You can change this at any time under Settings, without touching your wallet or its balance.
it.firstRunConnect.errEngine: The on-device engine could not start on this phone.
it.firstRunConnect.errEnterAddress: Enter the address of your wallet service (host:port, or an .onion).
it.firstRunConnect.title: Set up your wallet
it.firstRunConnect.intro: Nothing leaves this device until you tap. Pick where your wallet connects.
it.firstRunConnect.publicDesc: Fast, nothing to install. The wallet daemon can see your transactions.
it.firstRunConnect.torDesc: Hides your IP. The daemon still sees your transactions. Needs Orbot.
it.firstRunConnect.customDesc: A wallet daemon you run yourself.
it.firstRunConnect.changeLater: You can change any of this later in Settings, without touching your wallet or its balance.
it.orbotHelp.nativeIntro: The wallet reaches the onion through Orbot, the free Tor app. It isn't running:
it.orbotHelp.stepInstallIos: Install Orbot from the App Store.
it.orbotHelp.stepConnectIos: Open it and connect — Orbot runs as a VPN on iPhone, so allow the VPN configuration it asks for.
it.orbotHelp.stepVpnMode: Open it and turn on VPN mode.
it.orbotHelp.stepRetry: Come back and tap Connect over Tor again.
it.orbotHelp.desktopTitle: Tor isn't running on this computer
it.orbotHelp.desktopIntro: The wallet connects through Tor's own SOCKS port, so nothing has to be routed system-wide — Tor just has to be running. Start the Tor service, or simply open Tor Browser and leave it open, then try again.
it.orbotHelp.desktopPorts: It looks on 127.0.0.1:9050 (Tor service) and 127.0.0.1:9150 (Tor Browser).
it.orbotHelp.desktopOwnNode: For privacy without Tor, run your own node from the Node page — then nobody else sees what you ask.
it.orbotHelp.browserTitle: Open this wallet in Tor Browser
it.orbotHelp.browserIntro: An ordinary browser cannot reach an .onion address. The whole wallet is served over Tor — open it in Tor Browser at:
it.orbotHelp.browserKeys: Your keys stay on your device either way.
it.runOnPhoneOption.title: Run on this phone
it.runOnPhoneOption.desc: Most private. No daemon ever sees your transactions. A bit more battery.
it.runOnPhoneOption.nodeHint: Node to sync from — host:port. The default is the public ZKas node.
it.runOnPhoneOption.torDesc: Hides your IP from the node. Requires the Orbot app (Tor) running on this phone.
it.whatsNew.title: Recovery phrases
it.whatsNew.phraseDesc: New wallets use a standard BIP-39 phrase instead of a 64-character seed. Your existing seed keeps working.
it.whatsNew.accountsDesc: Add accounts from one phrase — one backup covers them all.
it.whatsNew.torDesc: Connect over an onion so the service never sees your IP.

th.history.recovering: Recovering your history from the chain — a minute or two. You can leave this tab.
th.history.empty: Nothing yet. Payments you receive and send show up here.
th.history.sentPrivately: Sent privately. Watch it confirm below — this updates live.
th.history.noticedOnOpen: Noticed when you opened the app
th.send.clipboardEmptyBody: Copy the address first, then tap Paste.

th.send.clipboardBlockedBody: Press and hold the address field, then choose Paste.
th.send.badAddress: That doesn't look like a zkas: address.
th.send.selfAddress: That's your own address. The payment works — it just returns to you, minus the fee.
th.send.feeHint: Leave empty and the wallet picks the fee. Raise it only after a fee error.
th.send.memoHint: Sealed inside the recipient's encrypted note — only they can read it. Never appears on-chain or on the explorer.
th.send.maturingHint: Only {{spendable}} is ready to spend right now — {{maturing}} is still arriving. Coins become spendable about 10 minutes after they land, including the change from a payment you just made. It'll be ready shortly.
th.send.notEnough: Not enough funds: {{spendable}} spendable, need {{need}} incl. up to {{maxFee}} fee.
th.send.feeSummary: + {{min}}–{{max}} fee (scales with how many coins get combined) = up to {{total}} total
th.send.catchingUp: Still catching up with the chain — you can pay once it finishes, so the wallet knows about all your coins.
th.send.warmBanner:
⚡ Your first payment will take a few minutes.
Locating your coins — this happens once. You can start the payment now.
th.sign.title: Sign message
th.sign.intro: Prove you control this wallet's address without spending. The signature discloses your viewing key (enables note detection, never spend authority).
th.verify.title: Verify message
th.verify.intro: Runs entirely in your browser — no server involved.
th.send.needSeed: This device doesn't hold this wallet's key yet. Enter your recovery phrase once to unlock sending here.
th.send.wrongSeed: That seed belongs to a different wallet — it does not unlock this one. Check which wallet you are restoring, or switch to the wallet that seed belongs to.
th.send.partialRecorded: {{message}} The part already broadcast is recorded in History.
th.send.manyNotes: Your balance sits in {{n}} notes. If this amount cannot fit in one transaction, nothing is sent and the wallet will offer consolidation or an explicit split payment.
th.send.memoSealed: “{{memo}}” — sealed in the recipient's encrypted note; only they can read it.
th.send.warmingNote: ⚡ This first payment will take a few minutes — the wallet has to locate your coins in the chain before it can spend them. It only does this once; later payments take seconds.
th.send.signedOnDevice: Verified and signed on your device, then broadcast. Usually takes a few seconds.
th.send.chooseSafely: Choose safely: consolidation is recommended. “Send in parts” broadcasts independent transactions; accepted parts cannot be automatically reversed if a later part fails.
th.send.consolidationSentBody: Wait for the new note to mature, then retry the full payment.
th.send.splitProgress: Your balance is spread across many small notes, so this payment is being sent as {{parts}} transactions — {{sent}} of {{total}} ZKAS confirmed so far. Keep this page open until it finishes.
th.send.title: Send
th.history.held_one: {{count}} outgoing transaction in flight — {{amount}} ZKAS temporarily held until it confirms (returned automatically within ~1 hour if it never does).
th.history.held_other: {{count}} outgoing transactions in flight — {{amount}} ZKAS temporarily held until it confirms (returned automatically within ~1 hour if it never does).
th.history.rescanHint: Re-read the chain to rebuild this history and recover any funds the local view lost.
th.history.recoveredNote: Recovered from the chain by your viewing key. Tap a payment for details.
th.history.exportFailed: Could not export the CSV on this device.
th.history.turnOffBody: Erases the stored transaction list only. Your balance and funds are unaffected.
th.daemonSetting.unreachable: Couldn't reach a wallet service at {{url}} ({{detail}}). Make sure zkas-walletd is running there and the port is open. Nothing was changed — still using {{current}}.
th.daemonSetting.title: Connect to your own node
th.daemonSetting.intro: Your seed always signs on this device. But the hosted service still sees your viewing key — it can watch your balance and history. To keep even that private, run zkas-walletd on your own node and connect this wallet straight to it.
th.daemonSetting.enterIp: Just enter your node's IP address — we add the rest.
th.daemonSetting.nativeTransports: The installed app supports HTTPS and plain HTTP LAN connections.
th.daemonSetting.webTransports: The web wallet requires HTTPS; use the installed app for plain HTTP on a LAN.
th.daemonSetting.portNote: Uses port {{port}} by default — add :port only if you changed it.
th.vaultSetting.title: Security & backup
th.vaultSetting.plaintextWarning: This wallet's seed is stored unencrypted on this computer — anyone who copies the file can spend your funds. Set a passphrase to encrypt it; your balance and history are untouched.
th.vaultSetting.lockingNote: Locking stops the daemon and forgets your passphrase until you re-enter it.
th.vaultSetting.lockBody: The wallet daemon stops and your passphrase is forgotten. You will need it again to unlock. Your funds are not affected.
th.autoConsolidationCard.title: Automatic consolidation
th.autoConsolidationCard.intro: Occasionally merges your oldest notes in the background so a payment always fits. Each merge costs a small fee — turn it off to merge yourself with Consolidate instead.
th.autoConsolidationCard.offNote: Off. A large payment may need splitting until you merge with Consolidate.
th.debugLogsCard.title: Debug logs
th.debugLogsCard.verboseHint: More detail from the on-device engine. Turn on when a wallet is stuck opening or a send fails, then Show engine logs.
th.debugLogsCard.noLogs: No logs yet — the engine may not be running.
th.networkPrivacyCard.title: Network privacy
th.networkPrivacyCard.desktopNote: Keys stay in this app. Strongest privacy: run your own node (Node page). You can also connect over Tor if Tor is running on this computer — both from Chain source above.
th.networkPrivacyCard.enterAddress: Enter a wallet-service address (host:port or an .onion).
th.networkPrivacyCard.intro: What your wallet connects to. Tap to switch.
th.networkPrivacyCard.publicHint: Fast. The wallet daemon can see your transactions.
th.networkPrivacyCard.torHint: Hides your IP. The daemon still sees your transactions. Needs Orbot.
th.networkPrivacyCard.customHint: A wallet daemon you run yourself.
th.backgroundSyncCard.title: Background sync
th.backgroundSyncCard.intro: While on, the phone wakes about every 15 min (even closed) to stay synced and notify you of payments. Off, it catches up when you open the app. The seed stays on this device either way.
th.backgroundSyncCard.onNote: On. Android may delay the wake when the battery is low — payments are never lost, the notification is simply later.
th.biometricToggle.linkIntroPin: Enter your current PIN once to link it to this device's fingerprint. It stays sealed on the device; the fingerprint only releases it to open the app.
th.biometricToggle.linkIntroPassphrase: Enter your current passphrase once to link it to this device's fingerprint. It stays sealed on the device; the fingerprint only releases it to open the app.
th.biometricToggle.isOn: Fingerprint unlock is on. Open the app with a fingerprint instead of typing.
th.biometricToggle.offerPin: Unlock with a fingerprint instead of typing your PIN.
th.biometricToggle.offerPassphrase: Unlock with a fingerprint instead of typing your passphrase.
th.appLockSetting.mismatch: The two entries do not match.
th.appLockSetting.wrongSecret: That passphrase does not unlock this device.
th.appLockSetting.title: App lock
th.appLockSetting.enableIntro: Choose what to unlock with. This encrypts the key of every wallet on this device and asks for it when the app opens — while locked, this device holds nothing that can spend any of them.
th.appLockSetting.alsoBioPin: Also unlock with fingerprint (you'll scan it once to link). Your PIN keeps working.
th.appLockSetting.alsoBioPassphrase: Also unlock with fingerprint (you'll scan it once to link). Your passphrase keeps working.
th.appLockSetting.backupFirstPin: Back up your wallet first. Nothing stores this PIN, so if you forget it the only way back in is your seed phrase or a backup file.
th.appLockSetting.backupFirstPassphrase: Back up your wallet first. Nothing stores this passphrase, so if you forget it the only way back in is your seed phrase or a backup file.
th.appLockSetting.pinStrength: A PIN stops someone who picks up your phone. Use a passphrase for stronger protection.
th.appLockSetting.disableIntroPin: Enter your current PIN to turn the lock off. Your key will be stored unencrypted on this device again.
th.appLockSetting.disableIntroPassphrase: Enter your current passphrase to turn the lock off. Your key will be stored unencrypted on this device again.
th.appLockSetting.onNotePin: On. Every wallet's key on this device is encrypted, and the app asks for your PIN to open. It re-locks itself after a few minutes in the background.
th.appLockSetting.onNotePassphrase: On. Every wallet's key on this device is encrypted, and the app asks for your passphrase to open. It re-locks itself after a few minutes in the background.
th.appLockSetting.offIntro: Your wallet keys are stored on this device unencrypted. Turn on a PIN or passphrase and every one of them is encrypted at rest, and the app asks for it on open — so someone holding this device, or a backup of its data, cannot spend from it.
th.switchWallet.title: Wallets
th.switchWallet.intro: This device can hold several wallets at once. Switching between them keeps every one of them — their keys, history and contacts stay exactly where they are.
th.restoreSeedBackup.passPlaceholder: The passphrase you gave the file
th.backupWallet.mismatch: The two passphrases do not match.
th.backupWallet.written: Backup written. Keep it off this computer — a USB stick or password manager. It is encrypted.
th.backupWallet.intro: Backup — save an encrypted copy of your wallet to a file. Restore it on any computer with this app. Give it its own passphrase; do not reuse the one that unlocks this device.
th.backupWallet.loseWarning: Lose this passphrase and the file cannot be opened — not by us, not by anyone. Your seed phrase remains the other way back in.
th.nodeSourceSetting.title: Wallet node
th.nodeSourceSetting.intro: The embedded wallet engine keeps your keys on this computer. Node changes are checked before the wallet switches.
th.desktopEngineDown.startingTitle: Starting the wallet on this computer
th.desktopEngineDown.startingBody: Loading your wallet and catching up to the chain. The first run takes a few minutes; it keeps going if you close this.
th.desktopEngineDown.lostTitle: Lost the connection to the wallet on this computer
th.desktopEngineDown.notStartedTitle: The wallet on this computer didn't start
th.desktopEngineDown.lostBody: The wallet is running on this computer but stopped answering. Retry reconnects to it.
th.desktopEngineDown.notStartedBody: The wallet that runs on this computer isn't answering. Your coins are safe on the chain — this is only how the app is reading them.
th.desktopEngineDown.publicHint: You can use the public wallet service instead: it has already scanned the chain, so nothing has to start or sync here.
th.desktopEngineDown.retryHint: If retrying does not help, the public wallet service above needs nothing running on this computer. You can switch back to running it here later, from Chain source.
th.setup.title: Can't reach the wallet service
th.setup.nativeDown: The wallet service isn't responding. Check your connection and try again shortly — your funds are safe on-chain.
th.setup.hostedDown: The hosted wallet service isn't responding. Nothing for you to run — try again shortly.
th.setup.privacyNote: Your spending key is on this device either way — it is never sent to the service. What running your own zkas-walletd changes is privacy: the hosted service can see which wallet is asking about which blocks, and your own daemon sees only what you already know.
th.setup.nativeTransports: The installed app accepts HTTPS and plain HTTP LAN addresses.
th.setup.webTransports: The web wallet requires an HTTPS wallet-service URL.
th.sendScene.warmingCaption: Preparing: locating your coins in the chain{{details}} — done once, never again
th.sendScene.signingCaption: Signing on your device — your key never leaves it
th.sendScene.broadcastingCaption: Sealed and shielded — broadcasting to the network
th.sendScene.slowCaption: Locating your coins in the chain — this can take a minute or two
th.sendScene.provingCaption: Building your zero-knowledge proof — nobody will see amount or recipient
th.sendScene.reassure: Nothing has been sent yet and nothing can be lost — keep this open.
th.txDetail.explorerNote: The explorer shows only that a shielded transaction happened — never its details.
th.accessTokenSetting.title: Show access-token field
th.accessTokenSetting.detail: Adds a token box to wallet-server setup. Only needed for a token-protected wallet server.
th.watchOnAnotherDevice.noKey: This device does not hold the key for this wallet.
th.watchOnAnotherDevice.intro: Your view key lets another device or tool watch this wallet — balance and history, read-only. It can never send.
th.watchOnAnotherDevice.warn: Anyone with this key sees every amount and memo this wallet has ever had, and everything it receives from now on — you can't undo that without moving your coins.
th.watchOnAnotherDevice.otherDevice: On the other device: open the wallet → Watch a wallet, then paste this key (or scan the QR).
th.stopWatching.intro: This device holds a view key and no spending key, so it can show the balance and history and cannot send. Nothing here can move coins.
th.stopWatching.warn: Removes the view key from this browser. Anyone else holding the link keeps their view — that can only be ended by moving the coins.
th.switchWallet.removeBody: This wallet's key and data are erased from this device. Your other wallets are not affected. The coins stay on-chain but are unreachable from here without a backup or seed phrase.
th.renameWallet.title: Rename wallet
th.deviceSeedBackup.noKey: This device holds no spending key for the wallet — it can watch the balance but not spend. Restore your seed phrase on the Send tab to spend from here.
th.deviceSeedBackup.mismatch: The two passphrases do not match.
th.deviceSeedBackup.copied: Your backup is copied. Paste it somewhere safe now — a password manager or a note to yourself.
th.deviceSeedBackup.written: Backup written. Keep it off this computer. It is encrypted, useless without the passphrase.
th.deviceSeedBackup.intro: Back up your wallet. Save an encrypted copy so you can restore this wallet if the machine is lost.
th.deviceSeedBackup.loseWarning: Lose the backup passphrase and the file cannot be opened — not by us, not by anyone. Your seed phrase remains the other way back in.
th.restoreSeedBackup.wrongWallet: That backup belongs to a different wallet than the one open now, so it was not applied — restoring it here would overwrite this wallet's key. Use “Add separate wallet”, then restore the backup there.
th.restoreSeedBackup.storeFailed: This device could not store the wallet key — free up space and try again.
th.restoreSeedBackup.restored: Wallet restored. Your balance rebuilds from the chain — this takes a minute or two.
th.restoreSeedBackup.intro: Restore from backup. Open an encrypted backup file and put its wallet on this computer.
th.saveContactDialog.storedOnDevice: Stored only on this device — a list of who you pay is exactly the metadata ZKas exists to protect.
th.contactsCard.title: Contacts
th.contactsCard.empty: Nobody saved yet. Naming an address here is the only way it will ever read as a person — the chain itself knows nothing about who anyone is.
th.editContact.name: Name
th.editContact.removeBody: Only the name is forgotten — any payments you made are untouched, and the address itself stays in your history.
th.rescanButton.offHint: Recovers your balance from the chain. History is off, so this rebuilds funds — not a transaction list.
th.rescanButton.rescanning: Rescanning — this tab updates as it catches up.
th.requestAmount.hint: The payer's wallet fills in the amount and note — they can still change them.
th.receive.title: Receive
th.receive.seedMoved: Looking for your recovery seed? It moved to Settings → Recovery seed, behind your app lock.
th.revealSeedCard.noKey: This device doesn't hold this wallet's key — it is never sent to the server. Restore it with your recovery phrase or backup.
th.revealSeedCard.introPhrase: These words restore this wallet and every account under it. Reveal only somewhere private.
th.revealSeedCard.introSeed: This seed is the only way to restore this wallet. Reveal only somewhere private.
th.revealSeedCard.privateWarn: Make sure nobody can see your screen. The next tap puts your spending key on it.
th.revealSeedCard.keepPrivate: Keep this private. Anyone with it controls your funds.
th.qrScanner.denied: Camera permission was denied. Allow camera access, or paste the address instead.
th.qrScanner.noCamera: No camera found on this device — paste the address instead.
th.qrScanner.failed: Couldn't start the camera. Paste the address instead.
th.qrScanner.hint: Point the camera at the recipient's address QR code
th.appearanceCard.title: Accent color
th.appearanceCard.intro: Balance, buttons and highlights. Teal is the ZKas signature.
th.signatures.title: Signatures
th.signatures.intro: Prove you control your address without spending from it, or check somebody else's proof.
th.aboutCard.title: About
th.aboutCard.blurb: ZKas Wallet — every balance and payment shielded by Orchard zero-knowledge proofs. Your spending key is held on this device and never sent anywhere.
th.contactPicker.title: Choose a contact
th.contactPicker.empty: No contacts yet. Save one after a payment, or from a received address — on a shielded chain the wallet is the only place an address can have a name.
th.saveContactDialog.title: Save contact
th.saveContactDialog.name: Name
th.connectionButton.addOwnDesc: A wallet daemon you run yourself.
th.connectionButton.notPairingCode: That code is not a wallet-service pairing code. On the computer serving the wallet, open Host → Network access → Pair a phone.
th.connectionButton.nodeNotInstalled: Managed local node is not installed yet. The Mine and Node screens can install the verified release automatically.
th.walletSwitcher.title: Your wallets
th.walletSwitcher.hintAccounts: Accounts share your phrase. Restoring on a new device? Add account brings each one back, in order.
th.walletSwitcher.hintSeparate: A separate wallet gets its own recovery phrase.
th.recoverHistoryDialog.title: Recover full history
th.recoverHistoryDialog.intro: Details are saved with this wallet, so anyone with its data can read them.
th.recoverHistoryDialog.knowWhenHint: Scan from that date. Much faster.
th.recoverHistoryDialog.heightKnown: Block height this wallet started at
th.recoverHistoryDialog.scanningFromDays_on: Scanning from DAA {{from}} — about {{count}} day of chain.
th.recoverHistoryDialog.scanningFromDays_ot: Scanning from DAA {{from}} — about {{count}} days of chain.
th.recoverHistoryDialog.scanningWhole: Scanning the whole chain. This finds everything, and takes the longest.
th.iosInstallNotice.installedCopy: Have a wallet in Safari? It is not shared with this installed copy — restore it here from its recovery phrase.
th.iosInstallNotice.beforeInstall: Installing to your Home Screen starts a separate, empty copy — back up your recovery phrase first, then restore it in the installed app.
th.connectionButton.engineStartFailed: The on-device engine could not start.
th.connectionButton.introDesktop: Your keys stay on this device either way. Use the public service for a wallet that is ready at once, or run the wallet here and pick the node it reads the chain from.
th.connectionButton.introMobile: Your keys stay on this device. Choose how it connects.
th.connectionButton.publicDescDesktop: Ready at once. The wallet daemon can see your transactions.
th.connectionButton.publicDescMobile: Fast. The wallet daemon can see your transactions.
th.connectionButton.thisComputerPublicDesc: Runs the wallet here. First sync scans the chain and takes a while.
th.connectionButton.torDescDesktop: Hides your IP. The daemon still sees your transactions. Needs Tor.
th.connectionButton.torDescMobile: Hides your IP. The daemon still sees your transactions. Needs Orbot.
th.consolidateDialog.errEnterSeed: Enter this wallet's 64-character recovery seed to sign on this device.
th.consolidateDialog.errWrongSeed: That seed belongs to a different wallet.
th.consolidateDialog.errNoAddress: This wallet has no address yet.
th.consolidateDialog.title: Manage notes
th.consolidateDialog.done: Done. Ready to spend after they settle (about 10 minutes).
th.consolidateDialog.more: Open this again once they settle to keep going.
th.consolidateDialog.split_one: Your balance is split into {{count}} note — the pieces it is made of. Fewer are cheaper to send; more let you pay a few times in a row.
th.consolidateDialog.split_other: Your balance is split into {{count}} notes — the pieces it is made of. Fewer are cheaper to send; more let you pay a few times in a row.
th.consolidateDialog.seedLabel: Recovery phrase · stays on this device
th.consolidateDialog.merged_one: Merged {{notes}} notes in {{round}} of about {{count}} pass
th.consolidateDialog.merged_other: Merged {{notes}} notes in {{round}} of about {{count}} passes
th.balanceHero.label: Shielded balance
th.balanceHero.ariaScanning: Scanning the chain for this wallet's notes
th.balanceHero.ariaRebuilding: Rebuilding this wallet's view of the chain
th.balanceHero.resuming: Opening — resuming from block {{block}}, nothing is lost
th.balanceHero.keepsGoing: You can close this and come back — it keeps going.
th.balanceHero.prunedRebuild: This node has pruned old history, so the rebuilt balance may come out a lower bound. Your coins are on-chain — rescan from a node that serves full history to see everything. If this is your own node and it is still filling in shielded history, wait for its log to say "shielded history: VERIFIED" and rescan.
th.balanceHero.prunedRebuildFrom: This node has pruned old history (available from block {{block}}), so the rebuilt balance may come out a lower bound. Your coins are on-chain — rescan from a node that serves full history to see everything. If this is your own node and it is still filling in shielded history, wait for its log to say "shielded history: VERIFIED" and rescan.
th.balanceHero.changeFromPayment: {{amount}} ZKAS coming back as change from your payment
th.balanceHero.changeOwnTx: {{amount}} ZKAS coming back from this wallet's own transaction
th.balanceHero.arriving: +{{amount}} ZKAS arriving — confirmed, settling into your wallet
th.balanceHero.sentOnWayMany: {{amount}} ZKAS sent — on its way · {{n}} payments
th.balanceHero.readyAndArriving: {{spendable}} ready to spend · {{maturing}} arriving — coins become spendable about 10 minutes after they land.
th.balanceHero.arrivingOnly: {{maturing}} arriving — you can pay once the wallet finishes checking the chain.
th.balanceHero.scanning: Balances appear as the wallet scans the chain — your funds are safe.
th.balanceHero.lowerBound: This balance is a lower bound: the wallet's view was rebuilt through a node that has pruned old history, so notes created long ago may be missing from it. Your coins are safe on-chain — rescan only from a node that serves full history (rebuilding through this one would come out just as blind). If this is your own node and it is still filling in shielded history, wait for its log to say "shielded history: VERIFIED" and rescan then.
th.balanceHero.lowerBoundFrom: This balance is a lower bound: the wallet's view was rebuilt through a node that has pruned old history (available from block {{block}}), so notes created long ago may be missing from it. Your coins are safe on-chain — rescan only from a node that serves full history (rebuilding through this one would come out just as blind). If this is your own node and it is still filling in shielded history, wait for its log to say "shielded history: VERIFIED" and rescan then.
th.addAccountWallet.noPhrase: This wallet has no recovery phrase, so an account cannot be derived from it. Use “Add separate wallet” — it gets its own recovery phrase, which you must back up.
th.addAccountWallet.errStore: could not store the account key
th.seedBackup.quizErr: That does not match. Check your written copy and try again.
th.seedBackup.legacyWarn: This wallet exists only on this device. No backup, no recovery.
th.seedBackup.verifyIntro: Pick each word from your written copy.
th.seedBackup.title: Write down your recovery phrase
th.seedBackup.warn: These 12 words restore your wallet. Anyone who has them owns the funds.
th.seedBackup.writeOnPaper: Write them on paper, in order.
th.seedBackup.alsoFile: Also save an encrypted backup file
th.recoverWallet.errNotSecret: That doesn't look like a recovery phrase (12 words) or a recovery seed (64 hex characters).
th.recoverWallet.errWrongSeed: That seed belongs to a different wallet. Check it and try again.
th.recoverWallet.errStore: This device could not store the wallet key — free up space and try again.
th.recoverWallet.watchIntro: Shows the balance and history without a recovery phrase. It cannot send: a view key carries no spending authority.
th.recoverWallet.viewKeyPlaceholder: paste the view key, or the whole link
th.recoverWallet.errNotViewKey: That is not a view key.
th.recoverWallet.title: Reconnect your wallet
th.recoverWallet.nothingLost: Nothing is lost. Your coins are safe on the chain. This browser no longer holds the key for this wallet — browsers clear stored site data (Safari does it after about a week without a visit), and the key was only ever here, never on the server.
th.recoverWallet.seedPlaceholder: Your recovery phrase, or the seed you saved
th.recoverWallet.knowWhen: Know roughly when this wallet was created? (much faster)
th.recoverWallet.wholeChain: Without this the whole chain is scanned. That finds everything, and takes the longest.
th.recoverWallet.checkedLocally: Checked on this device against the address above, and never sent anywhere.
th.recoverWallet.justWatch: Just watch this wallet instead (no phrase needed)
th.recoverWallet.homeScreen: To stop this happening again, add the wallet to your Home Screen — an installed app keeps its storage, a browser tab may not. The installed copy starts empty: enter the phrase there once, and it stays.
th.recoverWallet.notYours: Not your wallet? Create or import a different one
th.syncDestination.intro: Your wallet will sync through {{where}}. It sees your balance and history — never your keys, and it cannot spend.
th.onboard.errHasKey: This device already holds a wallet key. Restore that wallet instead — or use the wallet switcher's 'Add another wallet' so nothing is overwritten.
th.onboard.errStore: This device could not store the wallet key — free up space and try again.
th.onboard.errChooseBackup: Choose your backup .json file, or paste the backup text.
th.onboard.restoreIntro: Select the encrypted .json backup you saved, then enter its passphrase. The seed is decrypted on this device — the file and passphrase never leave it.

th.onboard.errClipboard: Couldn't read the clipboard — paste the backup into the box below instead.

th.noncustodial.fragmentedDefault: This payment needs more notes than one transaction can spend.
th.noncustodial.waitingPrevious: Waiting for the previous payment to finish preparing…
th.noncustodial.amountChanged: The daemon changed the requested amount. Refusing to sign.
th.noncustodial.couldNotPrepareComplete: The wallet service could not prepare the complete amount in one transaction.
th.noncustodial.feeAboveLimit: The daemon asked for a fee of {{fee}} ZKAS — above the {{max}} ZKAS this wallet allows. Refusing to sign.
th.noncustodial.partialSent: Sent {{sent}} ZKAS in {{n}} transactions, but {{owed}} ZKAS could not be sent: this wallet's balance is split across too many small notes. Consolidate the wallet and send the rest.

th.noncustodial.unsafeConsolidation: The wallet service returned an unsafe consolidation.
th.noncustodial.noSpendableToSplit: No spendable note is available to split right now. Wait for recent funds to mature (about 10 minutes), then try again.
th.noncustodial.fewerThanThree: Fewer than three notes are spendable right now, so consolidating would not reduce the wallet's note count.
th.status.behindDetail_one: You can send now — everything a payment needs is already in view. The wallet is still reading the newest {{n}} block, so anything that arrived in them is not counted yet.
th.status.behindDetail_other: You can send now — everything a payment needs is already in view. The wallet is still reading the newest {{n}} blocks, so anything that arrived in them is not counted yet.
th.status.behindDetailBare: You can send now — everything a payment needs is already in view. The wallet is still reading the newest blocks, so anything that arrived in them is not counted yet.

th.status.offlineDetail: Your coins are safe on the chain. The wallet will reconnect on its own.
th.status.openingDetail: Loading your wallet. This usually takes a few seconds.
th.status.readyToPayLabel: Ready to pay · still catching up
th.status.settingUpDetail: Reading the chain to find the coins that belong to you. The amount below is what it has found so far — it is not your final balance yet.
th.status.catchingUpDetail: Checking the chain for new payments. Your balance is up to date as of the last check.
th.status.finishingDetail: Your balance is up to date. The wallet is doing the last of its bookkeeping before it can pay — a few seconds.
th.status.warmingCountedDetail: Your balance is up to date. The wallet is locating your coins in the chain ({{pct}}%) — done once, never again; later payments take seconds.
th.status.warmingCountedDetailWaited: Your balance is up to date. The wallet is locating your coins in the chain ({{pct}}%) ({{waited}} so far) — done once, never again; later payments take seconds.
th.status.warmingDetail: Your balance is up to date. The wallet is getting ready to pay — the first payment is the slow one, later ones take seconds.
th.status.warmingDetailWaited: Your balance is up to date. The wallet is getting ready to pay ({{waited}} so far) — the first payment is the slow one, later ones take seconds.
th.status.readyDetail: Your balance is up to date.
